newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Easdaq says over 15 firms applied for admission.
newsitem.headline: Easdaq says over 15 firms applied for admission.

text.p: Europe's new growth stocks market Easdaq, which will be officially launched on Monday, said on Thursday it was now technically operational and more than 15 companies had applied for admission.
"A conservative estimate of 10 to 15 companies, some of them dual listings with Nasdaq, are expected to be quoted by the end of the year," it said in a statement.
Based in Brussels, Easdaq (European Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotation) will be a pan-European, quote-driven market based on screen trading.

Five companies in the process of being admitted are Belgian bio-tech firm Innogenetics, 12.5 percent owned by Kredietbank ; Belgian-based software firm Artwork Systems; German-based software firm Creatix; U.S.-based clinical testing firm UniHolding Corp ; and U.K-based vehicle management firm Pride Automotive Group.
Canada's Nasdaq-listed bio-tech firm DynaMotive Technologies has also said it plans to seek an Easdaq listing.

Modelled on New York's successful Nasdaq, where many European growth companies currently seek capital, Easdaq promises to give start-up firms access to a wider range of capital than their national stock markets can provide.

Share prices will be quoted in the currency chosen by the listed company. Business hours are Monday to Friday from 0930 to 1630 Central European Time, and trade reporting and matching facilities will be available 24 hours a day.
Easdaq said more than 30 financial institutions had applied for membership as dealers, market makers or sponsors.
However delays in translating the rules, which have been approved by Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt, means it is unlikely any stocks will be traded on day one.
Quotations would start gradually in October, and would initially be stocks already on Nasdaq, to be followed by initial public offerings once liquidity had built up, Easdaq said.
Easdaq has an agreement with Nasdaq to enable both markets to offer firms a dual trading facility.
To be admitted, firms must have total assets of 3.5 million Ecus ($4.43 million) and capital and reserves of two million Ecus. They must also be supported by at least two market-makers.
Easdaq envisages it will be quoting 50 stocks in 12 months' time, mounting to 500 in five years, though its business plan does not foresee breakeven until the fourth year of operations.
The project originated from contacts between the European Venture Capital Association, European Commission and various market players, and Nasdaq is one of its 91 shareholders.
Its traders are linked by a computer system modelled on TRAX, the International Securities Markets Association communications system, and deals will be settled by Switzerland's INTERSETTLE.
